The initializer has three active descriptors and a terminator. GameModeState defines preload as a byte kind separately from entry and exit callback pointers.
Canonical collection arguments, loop bounds and final call order match. An empty selection leaves the root untouched by this callback.
Later-node allocation failure returns the existing cursor while callers advance bookkeeping. The zero-count branch prevents an unconditional deduplication guarantee.

The producer timestamps and registers qualifying trophies before calling Toy_SetUnlockState with one. The callee adds to the active low-byte acquisition count with saturation; cleanup precedes tail termination.

The outcome/stocks guard and conditional return-mode request match source. The notification gate tests existence rather than selecting a destination; the supported-challenger table yields 5, 3, 1, then 0.

contradictions.reason: Accept the correction of the compiled-section claim: source object shape is established, but compiled section size and exclusive membership remain deferred without compiled evidence.
Accept correction of the scratch-purpose claim: pending zero-count trophies can qualify without a count increase.
Accept correction of preload-as-callback wording: preload is a byte kind, distinct from function pointers.
Accept the data-flow correction: cleanup and availability calls precede conditional termination, and unchanged-entry suppression has a zero-count exception.
Accept removal of complete/nonduplicating sequence guarantees: allocation failure can omit records despite advancing caller bookkeeping, and the trophy predicate admits zero counts.
Accept the state-behavior correction: trophy acquisition addition is not a boolean assignment, and cleanup occurs before tail termination.
Accept correction of the follow-up interpretation: a true notification gate establishes qualifying notices, not an already selected destination.
